title: Micro, meso and macro levels

draft.title: Micro, meso and macro levels
card: Researchers can study society at different scales. The scale they choose decides what they look at and what questions they ask.
the level of individuals and families. A study of how one family shares chores is at this level.
the level of groups and communities. A study of a local sports club or a town's neighbourhood is at this level.
the level of whole nations and the world. A study of migration across countries or national laws is at this level.
draft.remember: Micro is individuals and families, meso is groups and communities, macro is nations and the world.

a.q: Which study is at the meso level?
opts: How members of a Lismore surf club work together
How one teenager in Lismore talks with her parents
How Australian laws affect all schools in the country
How climate change affects people across the world
a.why: A surf club is a group, and groups and communities are the meso level. The teenager and her parents are an individual and a family, so that study is micro.
a.clue: Look for the option about a group, not one family or a whole nation.

b.q: Priya studies how a national government's changes to school funding affect schools across Australia. Which level is she studying?
opts: Macro, because it covers a whole nation
Meso, because it involves schools as groups
Meso, because it affects communities in some towns
b.why: The study looks at a national policy across the whole country, which is the macro level. Schools are groups, so meso is tempting, but the scale of the study is the nation, not one school or community.
b.clue: Ask how big the area being studied is, not just who is in it.

a.best: How members of a Lismore surf club work together

b.best: Macro, because it covers a whole nation
